citations.text: The entry labels Warring States forms of the cup graph as 木 with 不 supplying the sound, and identifies short strokes in the cited forms as decorative. It says Qin forms inherit the Warring States writing and sometimes expand 不 with 口 to 否. Its Han forms vary in both the meaning-side shape and sound-side writing. This is the book’s account of graphic development; it does not by itself settle the earliest form or establish that every later variant had the same components.

citations.text: The scan’s headword is 桮(杯). Its entry calls the Warring States forms phonosemantic, from 木 with 不 supplying sound, and says a horizontal stroke over 不 and short strokes in one graph are decorative. It says Qin forms continue the Warring States writing, with 不 sometimes elaborated by 口 into 否. The entry describes variation in Han forms and cites vessel uses, the measure phrase 一杯水 in Mencius, and other examples. These are the book’s claims and citations; they do not establish dates of the cited physical witnesses or a full semantic chronology.
